objective: Deploy 32653cac and prove BR-7 closure in production.
outcome: DEPLOYED AND PROVEN END TO END IN PRODUCTION, on a fully synthetic disposable account. BR-7 CLOSES on route (A): a real production account deletion erased real production evidence, and the recovery system refuses to resurrect it.

deployment.liveIdentityProof: FIVE STABLE READS of /health/ready all reporting gitCommit 32653cac2f04 with versionSourceStatus RENDER_GIT_COMMIT. The running service was re-read rather than the deploy job's success being taken as proof — the §310A/OPS-2 rolling-cutover lesson.
deployment.frontendNote: The backend service was deployed alone by pinned commit. No frontend deployment was triggered and none was needed: §313 changed backend source only.

productionProof.classificationTimingNote: On the pass that WRITES the tombstone the object still classifies as RECOVERY_ONLY_EXPECTED, because classification runs before the apply step. The next pass reports MISSING_LIVE_ERASURE_AUTHORIZED. Recorded rather than presented as the immediate state.

nonContamination.fiveRealObjects: UNCHANGED — verify-object-consistency --deep: 5 verified by full sha256 download, 0 missing, 0 size mismatches, 0 checksum mismatches, 0 orphans, CONSISTENT
nonContamination.sharedOwnershipExclusion: The synthetic account was owner-scoped, so the organisation-scoped object was never a candidate. The exclusion was verified by counting org-scoped rows before and after rather than by reasoning about the predicate alone.
nonContamination.residueLeftInProduction: One soft-deleted anonymised user row, one site and one inspection, all synthetic and named here. This follows the product's own documented retention policy — inspections and sites are retained as the compliance record — and matches the §300 precedent of naming a synthetic account rather than tidying it away. The evidence itself is gone.

rateLimiting.notWeakened: Nothing was disabled or raised for testing. The single production deletion returned HTTP 200, not 429, so it is a deletion result rather than a rate-limited one.

monitoring.mo1: CONFIGURED throughout; one alert dispatched at HTTP 200 during the interim ATTENTION_REQUIRED window when the synthetic object was briefly LIVE_UNBACKED — the monitor behaving exactly as designed
monitoring.expectedNonZero: MISSING_LIVE_ERASURE_AUTHORIZED = 1, which is the synthetic object and is the correct terminal state for an erased object.
